Definition: adverb from the same as G1675; Hellenistically, i.e. in the Grecian language:--Greek.
BiblicalUsage: Hellenisti means in the Greek tongue, and it appears twice, both times when Greek is the language of the moment. In Acts 21:37 Paul asks the chief captain, canst thou speak Greek, and in John 19:20 the title on the cross is written in Hebrew and Greek and Latin.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the two verses show why Greek mattered: it was the language a Roman officer and a Jewish crowd and a dying Saviour all shared, and the gospel would ride on it to the ends of the earth.
